title: Welcome back — reopening sessions after the app closes

steps.headline: How much design process should this feature go through before it is built?
steps.today: New screens normally go through a full route: these questions, then mockups, an outside tester who has never seen the plan, a signed list of what 'done' means, code reviewers and a final grade. Small, clear changes can skip straight to one before/after deck.
steps.problem: This screen is the first thing you would see after a crash, and it touches resuming, sessions open on your other computer, and local models. The full route catches more, but takes longer and uses more helpers.
steps.proposal: Pick the route. Either way you see mockups and a review deck before anything ships.

options.label: Full route
pros: An outside tester tries the mockups before you see them, and again after it is built.
A written 'definition of done' you sign, graded at the end.
Best fit for a screen that appears at startup, where a bug is very visible.
cons: Slower: several extra rounds before code.
Roughly a dozen helper runs, so more usage.

options.label: Short route
pros: Faster: I build it, then show you one before/after deck.
cons: No outside tester or grader, so more rides on your review.
Edge cases (other computer, local models) are more likely to slip through.

steps.intro: These decide which sessions appear on the Welcome back screen.

steps.path: Appears when you open the app
steps.headline: Only sessions where you sent at least one message come back.
steps.changed: Stated, not asked: a session you opened but never typed in is not remembered.
steps.notice: Empty 'New Session' tabs you forgot about do not clutter the list.

steps.path: Closing the whole app window while sessions are open
steps.headline: When you close the whole app on purpose with sessions open, should those come back next launch?
steps.today: Closing the app window with sessions open shows a warning that the sessions will be ended. Next launch opens on an empty start screen; the old sessions are only in the Resume browser.
steps.problem: A crash and a normal quit look alike afterwards. If normal quits count, you get the Welcome back screen after every quit; if they do not, a quit you regret loses your place.
steps.proposal: Three ways to treat a normal quit. Crashes, power loss and the computer shutting down always count.

options.label: Always come back
pros: Simplest: whatever was open is offered back, no matter how the app closed.
Matches 'the app closes or whatever'.
cons: If you often quit with sessions open, you see this screen most launches.

options.label: Ask in the quit warning
pros: The existing warning gains a 'Reopen these next time' tick box, so you decide at the moment you quit.
cons: One more thing to read every time you quit.
Slightly more to build and test.

options.label: Crashes only
pros: The screen appears only when something went wrong.
cons: A deliberate quit you regret means digging through the Resume browser.

steps.path: The X on a session tab
steps.headline: Closing one session with its X means you are done with it, so it never appears on Welcome back.
steps.changed: Stated, not asked: only the X on a single session removes it from the list. It stays in the Resume browser as today.
steps.notice: Sessions you closed one by one never reappear at startup.

steps.path: Using YouCoded on more than one computer
steps.headline: Each computer only offers back the sessions that were open on that computer.
steps.changed: Stated, not asked (you decided this on 2026-09-02): what was open on your laptop never shows up on your other computer's Welcome back screen.
steps.notice: If a session is now open on your other computer, the usual 'take it over?' question appears when you resume it, exactly as in the Resume browser today.

steps.page: What the screen looks like and does
steps.intro: The layout itself comes later as mockups. These set what it must be able to do.

steps.path: Appears when you open the app
steps.headline: Where should the list of sessions to reopen appear?
steps.today: After a restart the app opens on an empty start screen that says 'No Active Session', with a New Session form and a Resume button.
steps.problem: You have to remember what you were doing and hunt for each session in the Resume browser, one at a time.
steps.proposal: Three places the list could appear. Pick the one that feels right as the first thing you see.

options.label: Instead of start screen
options.summary: A full 'Welcome back' screen takes the start screen's place until you choose.
pros: Impossible to miss; room for a long list with titles, folders and times.
The usual start screen appears as soon as you finish.
cons: You must press a button (even 'Start fresh') before doing anything else.

options.label: Popup window
pros: Can be dismissed with Escape or a click outside.
The start screen is visible behind it.
cons: Easy to wave away by accident.
Less room; a long list scrolls in a small box.

options.label: Card on start screen
pros: Least intrusive; you can ignore it and start something new.
cons: Easiest to overlook, which defeats the point after a crash.
Crowds the start screen.

steps.path: The tick box beside each session
steps.headline: Should every session start ticked, ready to resume, or start unticked?
steps.today: There is no such list today.
steps.problem: After a crash you usually want most things back, but after a normal quit you may want only one or two.
steps.proposal: Pick the starting state. You can change any tick before pressing Resume.

options.label: All ticked
pros: One press gets everything back.
Best for the crash case.
cons: After a normal quit you untick the ones you don't want.

options.label: None ticked
pros: Nothing reopens unless you pick it.
cons: After a crash you tick every one by hand.

steps.headline: Besides resuming, what should you be able to do to each session on the list?
steps.today: The Resume browser can mark a session complete, which hides it there unless you ask to see completed ones.
steps.problem: Some sessions on the list are finished work you just never closed. Without a way to say so, they come back every time.
steps.proposal: Pick every action a row should offer. Resume, Resume all and Start fresh are there regardless.

options.label: Mark complete
pros: Same meaning as in the Resume browser: finished, hidden by default.
Tidies the Resume browser at the same time.
cons: None beyond a button per row.

options.label: Not now
options.summary: Take it off this list without marking it complete.
pros: For work that is not finished but not needed today; it stays findable in the Resume browser.
cons: A second button per row that looks similar to Mark complete.

options.label: Show in Resume browser
pros: Jump to the full browser to see notes, tags and preview.
cons: Leaves the Welcome back screen part-way through.

steps.headline: Sessions you leave unticked: forget them, or offer them again next launch?
steps.today: There is no such list today.
steps.problem: If unticked sessions come back every launch, the list never shrinks. If they are forgotten, a mis-click loses them from this list.
steps.proposal: Either way, forgotten sessions are still in the Resume browser.

options.label: Forget them
pros: The screen only ever shows what was open last time.
Nothing piles up.
cons: An unticked session is only reachable through the Resume browser afterwards.

options.label: Offer again
pros: Nothing drops off without a deliberate choice.
cons: The screen keeps appearing until you resume, complete or dismiss every row.

steps.path: Resuming a session that used a local or non-Claude model
steps.headline: When a session ran on a local or non-Claude model, should resuming it reuse that model automatically?
steps.today: Resuming such a session from the Resume browser first asks you which model to use.
steps.problem: Resuming five sessions at once could mean five model questions in a row.
steps.proposal: Pick whether Welcome back reuses the last model or asks.

options.label: Reuse last model
pros: One press resumes everything.
If that model is no longer available, it falls back to asking.
cons: You cannot switch model at resume time from this screen (you still can inside the session).

options.label: Ask each time
pros: Same as the Resume browser.
cons: A question per session when resuming several.

steps.headline: This ships on the desktop app first; the Android app gets it later.
steps.changed: Stated, not asked: on Android, sessions already keep running in the background when the app closes, and resuming old sessions there is not finished yet.
steps.notice: Nothing changes on your phone with this work.
